deep.reconstruction:
The page has two Fourier-type expansions of the inverse Gudermannian of the Jacobi amplitude, gd^{-1}(phi) = log tan(pi/4 + phi/2). There is no derivation on the page; the steps below are my reconstruction. Throughout, K = K(k), K' = K(k') and q = exp(-pi K'/K) is the nome belonging to k. Ramanujan does not state these definitions.

(1) Let u = F(phi,k) = 2K theta/pi, so phi = am(u,k) and theta = pi u/(2K). The page asserts
  log tan(pi/4 + theta/2) + 4 * sum_{n>=0} (-1)^n q^{2n+1} sin((2n+1)theta) / ((2n+1)(1 - q^{2n+1})) = log tan(pi/4 + phi/2).
[My derivation] d/du gd^{-1}(am u) = sec(phi) * dphi/du = dn u / cn u = dc u. The classical Fourier series is
  dc u = (pi/2K) sec(theta) + (2pi/K) * sum (-1)^n q^{2n+1} cos((2n+1)theta) / (1 - q^{2n+1}).
Integrate from 0 to u, using du = (2K/pi) dtheta:
- the sec term gives integral of sec(theta) dtheta = log tan(pi/4 + theta/2);
- the n-th cosine term gives 4(-1)^n q^{2n+1} sin((2n+1)theta) / ((2n+1)(1 - q^{2n+1})).
This is exactly the stated identity.

(2) Now let u = F(phi,k') = 2K theta'/pi, where K and q still belong to k. The page asserts
  theta' + 2 * sum_{n>=1} (1/n) q^n sinh(2n theta') / (1 + q^{2n}) = log tan(pi/4 + phi/2).
[My derivation] d/du gd^{-1}(am(u,k')) = dc(u,k'). By Jacobi's imaginary transformation, dc(u,k') = dn(iu,k). Put z = iu in the series dn(z,k) = pi/(2K) + (2pi/K) * sum q^n cos(n pi z/K)/(1 + q^{2n}). This gives
  dc(u,k') = pi/(2K) + (2pi/K) * sum q^n cosh(2n theta')/(1 + q^{2n}),  with theta' = pi u/(2K).
Integrating in theta' gives theta' + 2 * sum q^n sinh(2n theta')/(n(1 + q^{2n})), as stated.

The second series converges for |theta'| < pi K'/(2K), i.e. |u| < K'. This corresponds exactly to |phi| < pi/2, where the right-hand side is finite.

This is a self-contained note of two expansions of the type found in the elliptic-function chapters of Ramanujan's notebooks. It is unrelated to the previous page (binary products) and the next page (Rogers–Ramanujan / icosahedral material).
errors: No mathematical errors. Both identities check out under the implicit conventions: q = exp(-pi K'/K) with K, K' for modulus k, and K, q unchanged in the second formula even though the integral uses modulus k'.
These conventions, and the range of validity (|phi| < pi/2; in (2) equivalently |theta'| < pi K'/(2K)), are not stated on the page.

results.modern_name: Fourier series of gd^{-1}(am u) = log(nc u + sc u), the integrated Fourier series of dc u
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova, 1829); standard in Whittaker–Watson / DLMF 22.11 (dc expansion)

results.what: log tan(pi/4+phi/2) = theta' + 2 sum q^n sinh(2n theta')/(n(1+q^{2n})), with theta' = pi F(phi,k')/(2K)
results.modern_name: Imaginary (Jacobi) transformation of the Fourier series of dn, integrated; expansion of gd^{-1}(am(u,k')) in the complementary nome
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1829); classical consequence of the dn Fourier series and the imaginary transformation

deep.surprise_reason: Both are classical Jacobi-era Fourier expansions, obtained by integrating the series for dc u and for dn under the imaginary transformation. Similar entries appear in Ramanujan's notebooks; nothing here is new or ahead of its time.
